prf:sorting-color-energy:
Proof Proof of sorting color energy. Sorting deposits energy because a disordered pair sits in the antisymmetric eigenspace at eigenvalue -q^{-1}, and sorting lifts it to the symmetric eigenspace at eigenvalue q; the exchange must therefore pay the gap between the two. This is made precise by computing the projections onto each eigenspace.

(1) The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1 = 0 has roots q and -q^{-1} by the quadratic formula. The corresponding idempotents are:

  e_+ = \frac{\sigma_i + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}, \qquad
  e_- = \frac{q - \sigma_i}{q + q^{-1}}

with e_+ + e_- = 1 and e_+ e_- = 0. The image of e_+ is \mathrm{Sym}^2(V) (the symmetric representation, eigenvalue q); the image of e_- is \bigwedge^2(V) (the antisymmetric representation, eigenvalue -q^{-1}).

(2) A disordered pair occupies \bigwedge^2(V): the two items are in the wrong order, so the state is antisymmetric under exchange. Sorting swaps them into the correct order, moving the state to \mathrm{Sym}^2(V). This is the projection e_+. In the observation (observation), e_+ is the \mathrm{Ad} component: it acts on the colour fibre by conjugation, rotating the antisymmetric state to the symmetric eigenspace.

(3) The energy deposited is the eigenvalue difference: q - (-q^{-1}) = q + q^{-1}.

(4) Each adjacent transposition in the sorting algorithm corresponds to one braid crossing \sigma_i. The standard result from combinatorics: the minimum number of adjacent transpositions to realise \pi equals \mathrm{inv}(\pi), the number of pairs (i, j) with i < j and \pi(i) > \pi(j). Each crossing deposits q + q^{-1} in the colour fibre. \square

Example: three socks.

See Table.

At q = q_0: sorting three fully reversed socks costs 3 \times 2.011 = 6.033 action units in the colour fibre.
def:bundle-isotopy-equivalence:
Definition Isotopy equivalence of bundle initial conditions. Two bundle initial conditions are isotopy equivalent if they are related by a permutation of indices and an ambient isotopy within each fibre:

  \{(p_i, H_i)\}_{i \in I} \sim \{(p_{\sigma(i)}, H_{\sigma(i)}')\}_{i \in I}

where \sigma is a bijection on I and each H_{\sigma(i)}' is ambient-isotopic to H_{\sigma(i)} in the fibre E_{p_{\sigma(i)}}.
rem:bundle-isotopy-equivalence-remark: Remark Why bundle initial conditions are taken up to isotopy. The physical content of a bundle initial condition depends only on which hadron types are placed where, not on the index labels or the particular representative of each ambient isotopy class; isotopy equivalence identifies exactly the conditions with the same content.
def:torsion-knot-flow:
Definition Torsion-driven knot flow. Given a bundle initial condition \mathcal{S}_0 = \{(p_i, K_i)\}_{i=1}^{N}, the torsion-driven knot flow is the one-parameter family of bundle states

  \mathcal{S}_t = \bigl\{\bigl(\Phi_t^q(p_i), K_i\bigr)\bigr\}_{i=1}^{N} \qquad t \geq 0,

where \Phi_t^q is the flow on \mathbb{P}(V) generated by the q-deformed Reeb vector field \xi_q.

The flow has two components.

  1. Intrinsic rotation. Each knot type K carries an intrinsic angular momentum proportional to its crossing number c(K):

      \omega_K = c(K) \cdot \frac{2\pi}{[c(K)]_q!}

  2. Pairwise interaction. When two localized knots (p_i, K_i) and (p_j, K_j) are within Planck-scale separation d_{\mathbb{P}(V)}(p_i, p_j) < \ell_P, they experience a short-range repulsive force

      F_{ij} = \frac{\Delta_q(K_i) \cdot \Delta_q(K_j)}{d(p_i, p_j)^2 + \ell_P^2}

    where \Delta_q(K) is the q-Alexander polynomial of K evaluated at q = e^{-r}.
rem:torsion-knot-flow-remark:
Remark Conservation, naturality and archimedean content of the knot flow. The rotation term of the torsion-driven knot flow drives geodesic motion on \mathbb{P}(V) \cong S^2.

The flow preserves the total knot content \sum_i K_i but redistributes positions on \mathbb{P}(V). Categorically, the flow is a natural transformation on the category \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) of finite bundles over the projective line.

Archimedean specialisation. The combinatorial knot data lives over the ground ring R_q = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. The angular-momentum normalisation, the round metric on S^2, and the evaluation q = e^{-r} are the archimedean specialisation over \mathbb{R}.
rem:bundle-category:
Remark The category of finite bundles over \mathbb{P}(V). This category serves as the categorical counterpart of the Feynman path integral. Rather than integrating over all field configurations, the construction follows a single deterministic flow on a finite bundle. A configuration is a fixed collection of knots pinned to base points in the projective fibres. The content of the theory is the trajectory that configuration traces as the torsion flow carries it forward.

The bundle initial conditions and the torsion-driven knot flow define a category \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)):

  • Objects: Bundle initial conditions \mathcal{S}_0 = \{(p_i, K_i)\}.
  • Morphisms: Pairs (\sigma, \{\phi_i\}) consisting of a permutation \sigma \in S_N and a family of ambient isotopies \phi_i \colon K_{\sigma(i)} \simeq K_{\sigma(i)}' in the respective fibres. Morphisms preserve total knot content.
  • Identity: The identity permutation with trivial isotopies.
  • Composition: Permutation composition followed by isotopy concatenation.

The torsion flow \Phi_t^q is an endofunctor \Phi_t^q \colon \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) \to \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) acting on objects by moving base points and on morphisms by conjugating isotopies with the flow. The family \{\Phi_t^q\}_{t \geq 0} assembles into a continuous functor from (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, +) into the endofunctor category \mathrm{End}(\mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V))).
prose:outro-measurement-observation:
Chapter close — Measurement and observation.

This closes the measurement-and-observation chapter. Quarks reside in a Borromean configuration. Bundle initial conditions fix the observable's pre-state, the observation braid sorts colour by energy, and the bundle-category-level isotopy equivalence pins the measurement classes. Together, these constitute the bundle-structure picture, identifying observation as a categorical torsion-knot flow on the state bundle \mathcal{S}.

The final chapter of the main narrative (q-Geometric Langlands Correspondence) synthesises the fibre functor \tau, the Iwahori--Hecke operators of H_n(q), and the Kummer obstruction tower into an automorphic--spectral correspondence over the non-torsion locus of \mathbb{G}_m.
sec:q-gl-intro-prose:
Introduction to q-Geometric Langlands.

The aether parameter q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(k) = k^\times \setminus \mu_\infty (aether parameter) endows the differential calculus of a quantum observable universe with a one-parameter deformation. Two consequences govern this chapter:

  1. The q-deformed exterior derivative satisfies d_q^2 \neq 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2). This non-vanishing canonically obstructs the flatness of q-connections.
  2. The obstruction classes \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) (quantum characteristic classes) control the lifting of Frobenius--Hopf objects through the brane tower. Their Kummer filtration (Kummer filtration) isolates the arithmetic locus where q-flatness holds.

These structures assemble into a q-deformed Geometric Langlands correspondence. This equivalence is constructed as a \mathbb{G}_m-family of functors. The automorphic side consists of q-\mathcal{D}-modules on the moduli of G_q-bundles. The spectral side consists of quasi-coherent sheaves on the moduli of q-local systems for the Langlands dual \check{G}_q. The rigid fibre functor \tau (fibre-functor rigidity) mediates the equivalence via Tannaka--Krein reconstruction. This family is well-defined on the non-torsion locus \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}} but degenerates at roots of unity where [n]_q = 0. The perpetual obstruction (Kummer filtration) ensures the correspondence remains intrinsically non-torsion.
sec:q-local-systems-intro: This section establishes the automorphic-side geometry upon which the q-Hecke correspondences act. It defines q-local systems on a brane curve X and the q-flat connections that supply their q-holonomy residues.
def:q-local-system:
Definition q-Local system. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(k) (aether parameter), and let X be a brane curve. A q-local system on X with structure group G_q is a functor

  \mathcal{L}_q \colon \Pi_1(X) \longrightarrow \mathbf{Rep}(G_q)

from the fundamental groupoid \Pi_1(X) to the category of finite-dimensional representations of G_q. This functor must satisfy the q-monodromy condition: for every contractible loop \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathbf{1} in \Pi_1(X), the monodromy obeys

  \mathcal{L}_q(\varrho) = \mathrm{id} + (q - 1)\Omega_q(\varrho),

where \Omega_q(\varrho) \in \mathrm{End}(\tau(\mathcal{L}_q)) is the q-holonomy residue determined by the underlying q-connection.

The q-monodromy condition reflects the local geometry of the \mathbb{G}_m-family. At q = 1, the residue vanishes and \mathcal{L}_1 reduces to a classical flat bundle. For q \neq 1, the non-vanishing curvature d_q^2 \neq 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2) obstructs trivial monodromy. The Kummer reduction of the obstruction class \kappa_0 at level n (Kummer filtration) controls lifting through the brane tower. A q-local system \mathcal{L}_q lifts from level n to n+1 if and only if \kappa_0 \equiv 0 \pmod n, which occurs precisely when n \mid \chi(A). The moduli stack of q-local systems on X is denoted \mathrm{LocSys}_{G_q}(X).
rem:q-local-system:
Remark From monodromy to q-monodromy. Classical local systems correspond to representations of \pi_1(X) because their connections satisfy d^2 = 0. In a quantum observable universe, the perpetual curvature d_q^2 \neq 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2) obstructs naive flatness. The q-monodromy condition absorbs this obstruction. For contractible loops, parallel transport deviates from the identity by a residue proportional to (q-1).

The Kummer filtration measures this deviation at finite levels. An obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) vanishes modulo n precisely when n \mid \chi(A) (Kummer filtration). At these levels, the q-monodromy becomes n-divisible, determining a sublocus of \mathrm{LocSys}_{G_q}(X) with enhanced lifting properties through the brane tower. When n \nmid \chi(A), the obstruction forces a non-trivial q-holonomy residue on every q-local system. This behavior mirrors the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0, where the symmetric group relation (T-1)(T+1) = 0 deforms to split braiding eigenvalues from \pm 1 to q and -q^{-1}.
def:q-flat-connection:
Definition q-Flat connection. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe and let \mathcal{V} be a G_q-equivariant object in \mathbf{C} over the brane curve X. A q-flat connection on \mathcal{V} is a q-connection \nabla_q \colon \mathcal{V} \to \Omega^1_q \otimes \mathcal{V} (categorical q-connection) whose total curvature \nabla_q^2 equals the intrinsic q-curvature determined by d_q^2:

  \nabla_q^2 = (q - 1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}.

Here, \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{V}) \otimes \Omega^2_q is the intrinsic q-curvature, defined as the image of the obstruction class \kappa_0 under the Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg map (Kummer filtration):

  \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}
  = 
  \mathrm{HKR}^{-1}(\kappa_0)
   \in 
  HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}).
rem:q-flat-connection:
Remark The d_q^2 \neq 0 obstruction as curvature. A q-flat connection carries the minimal possible curvature compatible with the q-deformation: curvature arising solely from the perpetual d_q^2 obstruction rather than from any connection form. It is not flat in the classical sense (\nabla_q^2 \neq 0 in general). When \kappa_0 \neq 0 (the perpetual obstruction), q-flat connections exist but have non-zero total curvature (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}.

The condition \nabla^2 = 0 provides the geometric incarnation of d^2 = 0. The q-flatness equation \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} absorbs the canonical obstruction to flatness. The Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg comparison (Kummer filtration) identifies the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} with the gerbe-theoretic obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m). The Kummer filtration pulls back to a filtration on HH^2 that measures the n-divisibility of the q-curvature.

The HKR identification. The Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg comparison (Kummer filtration) identifies the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q with the obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m). The deformation-theoretic obstruction HH^2 and the gerbe class in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) are two views of the same class. The Kummer filtration on the target pulls back to a filtration on HH^2 measuring n-divisibility of the q-curvature.

The perpetual obstruction and Hecke commutativity. From the Hecke perspective, the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q is the categorical shadow of the non-commutativity of Hecke operators at different places: classically Hecke operators at distinct points commute, but the q-deformation introduces (q-1)-proportional commutators. The perpetual obstruction (Kummer filtration) ensures this non-commutativity persists at cofinitely many Kummer levels.

Classical limit, curvature decomposition and q-local systems. In the classical limit q \to 1, the prefactor (q - 1) vanishes, so the intrinsic term drops out and q-flatness reduces to ordinary flatness (\nabla_q^2 = 0); the residual curvature is present only when q \neq 1.

In general, a q-connection has total curvature

  \nabla_q^2 = (q - 1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} +
  \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}},

where \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}} is the connection-dependent curvature — the contribution from the connection form itself. A q-connection is q-flat when \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}} = 0: all curvature is intrinsic, arising solely from the d_q^2 \neq 0 obstruction (non-vanishing of d_q^2).

The category of q-flat connections on X with structure group G_q is equivalent to the category of q-local systems \mathrm{LocSys}_{G_q}(X) (q-local system).
sec:q-hecke-correspondences-intro: Building on the moduli of q-local systems, the q-Hecke operator is constructed: a Hecke modification twisted by the Iwahori–Hecke generators \sigma_i. This operator acts on the moduli of G_q-bundles. A q-Hecke eigensheaf diagonalises this action, with eigenvalues landing in the representation ring of the dual group. The rigid fibre functor \tau extracts these eigenvalues as characters, matching the automorphic side to the spectral side in the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence.
def:q-hecke-operator:
Definition q-Hecke operator. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with brane curve X and quantum gauge group G_q (quantum gauge group). Let x \in X be a closed point and \lambda a dominant coweight of G_q. The q-Hecke operator \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} is the integral transform

  \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} \colon
  \mathcal{D}_q\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G_q})
  \longrightarrow
  \mathcal{D}_q\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G_q})

defined by the q-Hecke correspondence:

\begin{tikzcd}
  & \mathrm{Hecke}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} \arrow[dl, "h_\leftarrow"'] \arrow[dr, "h_\rightarrow"] & \\
  \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X) & & \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X)
\end{tikzcd}

Here, \mathrm{Hecke}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} parametrises pairs (\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}') of G_q-bundles on X equipped with an isomorphism \mathcal{P}|_{X \setminus x} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{P}'|_{X \setminus x} of relative position \lambda.
rem:q-hecke-operator-remark:
Remark Hecke relation for the q-Hecke operators. The q-Hecke operators satisfy the Iwahori--Hecke algebra relation (braiding eigenvalues):

  (\mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} - q)
  (\mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} + q^{-1}) = 0.

They act with eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} on the symmetric and antisymmetric channels, respectively.
def:q-hecke-eigensheaf:
Definition q-Hecke eigensheaf. A q-\mathcal{D}-module \mathcal{M} on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X) is a q-Hecke eigensheaf with eigenvalue \mathcal{L}_q \in \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X) if it admits functorial isomorphisms

  \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M})
  \simeq
  \mathcal{M} \otimes V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x

for every closed point x \in X and every dominant coweight \lambda. Here, V_\lambda^{(q)} is the irreducible representation of \check{G}_q of highest weight \lambda, and V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x is its fibre at x under the q-local system \mathcal{L}_q (q-local system).

These isomorphisms must be compatible with:

  1. Tensor products: The isomorphism for \lambda + \mu is the composition of the isomorphisms for \lambda and \mu, twisted by the braiding \sigma_q \colon V_\lambda^{(q)} \otimes V_\mu^{(q)} \to V_\mu^{(q)} \otimes V_\lambda^{(q)}.
  2. Factorisation: For distinct points x \neq y, the Hecke operators commute up to a (q-1)-correction: [\mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}, \mathbf{T}_{y,\mu}^{(q)}] = O(q-1).
prop:q-hecke-eigenvalue:
Proposition q-Hecke eigenvalues from the fibre functor. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q. Let \mathcal{M} be a q-Hecke eigensheaf on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X) (q-Hecke eigensheaf). Its eigenvalue \mathcal{L}_q \in \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X) is uniquely determined by the action of \tau on the Hecke eigenvalue data:

  \mathcal{L}_q \simeq
  \mathrm{Aut}^\otimes(\tau)\text{-}\mathrm{equivariantisation of }
  \big\{ V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x \big\}_{\lambda, x}.

The rigidity of the fibre functor (fibre-functor rigidity) implies that this collection of Hecke eigenvalues determines \mathcal{L}_q up to unique isomorphism.
prf:q-hecke-eigenvalue:
Proof Proof of q-Hecke eigenvalue determination. By Tannaka--Krein reconstruction, the fibre functor \tau on \mathbf{Rep}(\check{G}_q) recovers the quantum group \check{G}_q as \mathrm{Aut}^\otimes(\tau). A \check{G}_q-local system \mathcal{L}_q is equivalent to a tensor functor \mathbf{Rep}(\check{G}_q) \to \mathrm{Vect}_X. This functor is uniquely determined by the fibre data \{V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x\} over all coweights \lambda and points x.

The Hecke eigensheaf property provides exactly this data. For each (\lambda, x), the eigenvalue isomorphism \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \simeq \mathcal{M} \otimes V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x extracts the fibre V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x as a multiplicity space.

The tensor compatibility of the Hecke isomorphisms ensures that the assignment V_\lambda^{(q)} \mapsto V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x is a tensor functor. It thus defines a point of \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X). The rigidity of \tau (fibre-functor rigidity) guarantees that any two tensor functors with isomorphic fibre data are uniquely isomorphic. \square
sec:q-gl-conjecture-intro:
The failure of the quantum differential to square to zero organises this section. The obstruction it measures is what confines the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence to the non-torsion locus: the correspondence is well-defined only where that obstruction is controlled, and each result below either quantifies the obstruction or works within that locus. The construction is abstract, but the next section makes it concrete by instantiating the correspondence as q-opers.

The section opens with the Definition: q-Langlands dual group, the deformation of the classical dual that carries the aether parameter on the spectral side. The Conjecture: q-Geometric Langlands correspondence then states the equivalence itself — between q-\mathcal{D}-modules on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q} and quasi-coherent sheaves on \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}, well-defined on the non-torsion locus. The Proposition: Obstruction to q-flatness and its proof calibrate the conjecture: they compute the Yekutieli obstruction classes and exhibit them as the precise aether-theoretic measure of the failure of d_q^2 = 0.

The section closes with two structural conjectures organised by this obstruction. The Conjecture: Kummer filtration on q-local systems reads the Kummer reduction as the level-n lifting obstruction of q-local systems through the brane tower, pinning the correspondence to the arithmetic locus where the quantum integer [n]_q is nonzero. The Conjecture: Fibre-functor mediation of the q-Langlands correspondence asserts that the rigid fibre functor implements the equivalence by Tannaka–Krein reconstruction, with the Remark: Proof sketch for fibre-functor mediation outlining the argument the next section instantiates concretely for q-opers.
def:q-langlands-dual:
Definition q-Langlands dual group. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with quantum gauge group G_q. The q-Langlands dual group of G_q is

  \check{G}_q = G_{q^{-1}}^{\vee},

where (-)^\vee denotes the classical Langlands dual.
rem:q-langlands-dual-remark:
Remark The q-Langlands dual of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) and the inversion q \mapsto q^{-1}. For G_q = \mathrm{SU}_q(2) (quantum \mathrm{SU}(2)), the q-Langlands dual group is

  \check{G}_q = \mathrm{SU}_{q^{-1}}(2) \cong \mathrm{SO}_{q^{-1}}(3).

The duality relates \check{G}_q to G_q by root system duality together with the inversion q \mapsto q^{-1}. The root system of \mathrm{SU}(2) is self-dual. The inversion q \mapsto q^{-1} interchanges the two eigenvalues of the braiding: q \leftrightarrow -q^{-1}. This exchanges the symmetric and antisymmetric channels of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra. It represents the categorical manifestation of exchanging roots and coroots. In the \mathbb{G}_m-family picture, the Langlands involution is the inversion automorphism \iota(q) = q^{-1}. This preserves the torsion subgroups \mu_n and acts as the identity on \mu_2.
def:q-oper:
Definition q-Oper. Let \check{G}_q be the q-Langlands dual group (q-Langlands dual) and let \check{\mathfrak{b}}_q \subset \check{\mathfrak{g}}_q be a Borel subalgebra. A q-oper on X is a q-flat connection (q-flat connection)

  (\mathcal{P}_{\check{G}_q}, \nabla_q)

on a \check{G}_q-bundle \mathcal{P}_{\check{G}_q} \to X, equipped with a \check{B}_q-reduction \mathcal{P}_{\check{B}_q} \subset \mathcal{P}_{\check{G}_q}. This data must satisfy the q-oper condition: the q-connection \nabla_q is strictly transverse to the Borel reduction. Specifically, for each simple root \alpha_i of \check{G}_q, the component of \nabla_q along \check{\mathfrak{g}}_{-\alpha_i} must not vanish:

  \mathrm{pr}_{-\alpha_i}(\nabla_q \bmod \check{\mathfrak{b}}_q)
  \neq 0.

The moduli stack of q-opers is denoted \mathrm{Op}_{\check{G}_q}(X).
rem:q-oper-remark: Remark Rank-2 q-opers as q-Sturm--Liouville operators. For a q-oper in the rank-2 case \check{G}_q = \mathrm{SU}_{q^{-1}}(2), a q-oper on a brane curve X is a rank-2 q-flat bundle with an invariant line subbundle \mathcal{L} \subset \mathcal{V} satisfying the transversality condition \nabla_q(\mathcal{L}) \not\subset \mathcal{L} \otimes \Omega^1_q. This geometric data is equivalent to a q-deformed Sturm--Liouville operator \partial_q^2 + t(z), where t(z) \in H^0(X, (\Omega^1_q)^{\otimes 2}), providing the rigid spectral data dual to q-Hecke eigensheaves.
conj:q-geometric-langlands:
Conjecture q-Geometric Langlands correspondence. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with brane curve X, quantum gauge group G_q, and q-Langlands dual \check{G}_q (q-Langlands dual).

The correspondence below is the aether-level analogue of geometric Langlands: it relates \mathcal{D}_q-modules on the quantum bundle stack to quasi-coherent sheaves on the moduli of local systems for the q-dual, so that spectral data on one side controls automorphic data on the other. At the classical value q = 1 it specialises to the ordinary geometric Langlands equivalence (property 5 below), which fixes the target that the deformed statement must recover; the parameter q then deforms that equivalence across the non-torsion locus of the aether. With this anchor in hand, the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence asserts the existence of an equivalence of \infty-categories:

  \mathbb{L}_q \colon
  \mathcal{D}_q\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X))
  \xrightarrow{ \sim }
  \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X)).

This equivalence is parametrised by the non-torsion locus q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(k) and satisfies five properties:

  1. Hecke compatibility: For every q-Hecke operator \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} (q-Hecke operator), \mathbb{L}_q intertwines the action on the left with the action of V_\lambda^{(q)} on \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X):

      \mathbb{L}_q \circ \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}
  \simeq
  V_\lambda^{(q)}(-)_x \otimes \mathbb{L}_q.

    This is the eigensheaf-matching condition: intertwining the q-Hecke action with tensoring by V_\lambda^{(q)} is what makes \mathbb{L}_q a Langlands correspondence rather than an arbitrary equivalence of categories.

  2. Fibre-functor factorisation: the equivalence factors through the fibre functor \tau:

      \mathbb{L}_q = \tau^* \circ \mathbb{L}_q^{\mathrm{Tannakian}}.

    where \mathbb{L}_q^{\mathrm{Tannakian}} is determined by Tannaka--Krein reconstruction for \check{G}_q. Routing the equivalence through \tau keeps it compatible with the observation frame, so that the dual group is recovered from its representation category rather than posited independently.

  3. q-Oper locus: the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q restricts to a bijection between q-opers (q-oper) and q-Hecke eigensheaves (q-Hecke eigensheaf):

      \mathrm{Op}_{\check{G}_q}(X)  \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X)
  \quad\xrightarrow{\mathbb{L}_q^{-1}}\quad
  \{\text{\(q\)-Hecke eigensheaves}\}.

    This pins down which local systems arise as q-Hecke eigensheaves: the q-opers cut out the distinguished spectral parameters that the eigensheaves correspond to under \mathbb{L}_q.

  4. Kummer constraint: the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q is well-defined as a \mathbb{G}_m-family on the non-torsion locus \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}. At roots of unity q \in \mu_n the quantum dimension [n]_q = 0 vanishes, the Frobenius pairing degenerates, and \mathbb{L}_q degenerates. The obstruction (Kummer filtration) persists at all Kummer levels n \nmid \chi(A).

  5. Classical limit: as q \to 1, \mathbb{L}_q recovers the classical Geometric Langlands equivalence [frenkel2007].

Relation to the quantum q-Langlands correspondence of Aganagic, Frenkel, and Okounkov. Mina Aganagic, Edward Frenkel, and Andrei Okounkov [aganagic2018] establish a quantum q-Langlands correspondence on genus-zero curves (\mathbb{P}^1 and \mathbb{C}^\times with tame ramification), relating conformal blocks of the quantum affine algebra U_\hbar(\widehat{{}^L\mathfrak{g}}) to deformed \mathcal{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})-algebra blocks across a two-parameter deformation (q, t) whose q \to 1 limit (at fixed level parameter \beta with t = q^\beta) recovers the quantum geometric Langlands correspondence. The conjecture stated above is a different single-parameter formulation rather than a special case of that theorem: it is posed on a compact higher-genus brane curve X (principally Bring's curve of genus g = 4, which admits no global multiplicative shift z \mapsto qz), deforms the differential along the contact-Reeb splitting d_q via the single aether parameter q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}, and specializes directly at q \to 1 to the classical (non-quantum) geometric Langlands equivalence.
prop:q-gl-obstruction-calc:
Proposition Obstruction to q-flatness. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with \chi(A) \neq 0 and obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) (quantum characteristic classes). Assume:

  • (H-HKR) the Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg comparison identifies the space of intrinsic q-curvatures HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) with H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m), by an isomorphism \Theta sending the intrinsic curvature to \kappa_0;
  • (H-tr) the trace \mathrm{tr} \colon H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) \to \mathbb{Z} is an isomorphism, with \mathrm{tr}(\kappa_0) = \chi(A).

Then:

  1. The intrinsic q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} = \Theta^{-1}(\kappa_0) \in HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) is non-zero whenever \kappa_0 \neq 0.
  2. A q-connection \nabla_q is q-flat (q-flat connection) when its connection-dependent curvature \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}} vanishes. This condition does not involve \kappa_0, so q-flat connections can exist when \kappa_0 \neq 0; they then carry the intrinsic curvature of item 1. Lifting a q-flat connection through the brane tower to level n requires \kappa_0 \equiv 0 \pmod n, that is, \kappa_0 \in n\,H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).
  3. At Kummer level n, the class \kappa_0 \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)/n vanishes if and only if n \mid \chi(A). Thus q-flat G_q-connections lift to level n only when n divides |\chi(A)|.
  4. For \chi(A) \neq 0, the condition \kappa_0 \not\equiv 0 \pmod n holds at a density-1 set of Kummer levels n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}; this is the perpetual obstruction. The q-local systems exist as objects with intrinsic curvature, but their brane tower lifts are obstructed at cofinitely many levels.

The reduction is taken in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)/n, not in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n): the Kummer sequence embeds H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)/n in H^3(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n).
prf:q-gl-obstruction-calc:
Proof Proof of the obstruction to q-flatness. Item (1). The q-flatness equation is \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q (q-flat connection). Its intrinsic part \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} is a class in HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}). HKR alone relates polyvector fields to Hochschild cohomology; it does not identify HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) with H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m). That identification is hypothesis (H-HKR), under which \Theta(\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}) = \kappa_0 = e(\xi) (Kummer filtration). Since \Theta is injective, \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} \neq 0 whenever \kappa_0 \neq 0.

Item (2). q-flatness is the vanishing of the connection-dependent part \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}}, while \kappa_0 determines the intrinsic part \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} (item 1). The two are separate, so \kappa_0 \neq 0 does not prevent q-flatness; it only makes the intrinsic curvature non-zero. The lifting requirement is the quantum lifting condition: lifting from level n needs \kappa_n = 0, and \kappa_n \equiv \kappa_0 \pmod n, which gives \kappa_0 \in n\,H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

Item (3). By (H-tr), \mathrm{tr} induces an isomorphism H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)/n \cong \mathbb{Z}/n sending \kappa_0 \bmod n to \chi(A) \bmod n. So \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0 if and only if n \mid \chi(A). Without (H-tr) the trace alone would not determine the class. The complementary subgroup structure \kappa_n = \kappa_0 + \delta_n prevents cancellation.

Item (4). The set \{n : n \mid \chi(A)\} has exactly d(|\chi(A)|) elements, where d is the divisor function. This set is finite. Its complement in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} has density 1. \square
conj:q-gl-kummer-filtration:
Conjecture Kummer filtration on q-local systems. The Kummer tower \mu_1 \subset \mu_2 \subset \cdots \subset \mu_\infty \subset \mathbb{G}_m (Kummer filtration) induces a descending filtration on the moduli of q-local systems. For each n \geq 1, define the level-n sublocus:

  \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}^{(n)}(X)
  \subset
  \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X).

This sublocus consists of q-local systems \mathcal{L}_q whose q-monodromy \Omega_q(\varrho) (q-local system) is n-divisible in \mathrm{End}(\tau(\mathcal{L}_q)) for every contractible \varrho.

  1. \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}^{(1)}(X) = \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X) (all q-local systems).
  2. The q-GL equivalence \mathbb{L}_q (q-GL conjecture) restricts to each filtered piece: 
      \mathbb{L}_q^{(n)} \colon
  \mathcal{D}_q^{(n)}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G_q})
  \xrightarrow{ \sim }
  \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}^{(n)}(X)).
    Here, \mathcal{D}_q^{(n)} consists of q-\mathcal{D}-modules whose Hecke eigenvalues have n-divisible monodromy.
  3. The sublocus \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}^{(n)} admits lifts through the brane tower only when n \mid \chi(A) (obstruction calculation). At levels n \nmid \chi(A), the perpetual obstruction prevents full lifting.
  4. The q-GL equivalence \mathbb{L}_q is well-defined as a \mathbb{G}_m-family on \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}} = \mathbb{G}_m \setminus \mu_\infty.
conj:q-gl-fiber-functor:
Conjecture Fibre-functor mediation of the q-Langlands correspondence. Under the hypotheses of the q-Geometric Langlands conjecture, the Tannakian rigidity of the fibre functor \tau pins the correspondence: it forces \tau to determine the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q uniquely up to natural isomorphism:

  \mathbb{L}_q(\mathcal{M})(\mathcal{L}_q)
  \simeq
  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Rep}(\check{G}_q)}
  \big(\tau(-),
  \mathrm{Hecke}_q(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{L}_q)\big).

where \mathrm{Hecke}_q(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{L}_q) is the tensor functor V_\lambda^{(q)} \mapsto \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \otimes \mathcal{L}_q(V_\lambda^{(q)})_x^* encoding all Hecke eigenvalue data simultaneously. Evaluated at a single dominant weight \lambda, the right-hand side is the Hom-set into \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \otimes \mathcal{L}_q(V_\lambda^{(q)})_x^* — the Hecke eigenvalue datum at that one \lambda; letting \lambda range over all dominant weights assembles these single-weight data into the equivalence above.

This uniqueness is the Tannakian rigidity of \tau (fibre-functor rigidity): any two equivalences compatible with the Hecke eigensheaf structure and the fibre functor are connected by a unique natural isomorphism.
rem:q-gl-fiber-functor-sketch:
Remark Proof sketch for fibre-functor mediation. The equivalence is pinned by the Tannakian rigidity of the fibre functor \tau: once \tau is fixed, reconstructing the dual group, transporting the Hecke datum, and closing uniqueness admit no freedom. The proof realises this in three steps.

Concretely, the archetype to keep in mind is a rank-one q-local system \mathcal{L}_q together with the single q-Hecke eigensheaf it governs; the general statement replaces this pair by the full tensor categories on either side.

Step 1: Tannakian reconstruction of \check{G}_q. By fibre-functor rigidity, the fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{Rep}(G_q) \to \mathrm{Vect} is unique up to unique isomorphism. Tannaka--Krein reconstruction gives G_q \cong \mathrm{Aut}^\otimes(\tau). Applying root-system duality and inversion q \mapsto q^{-1} yields \check{G}_q and its canonical fibre functor \check{\tau}.

Step 2: Hecke data determines \mathbb{L}_q. Let \mathcal{M} be a q-Hecke eigensheaf with eigenvalue \mathcal{L}_q. The collection of isomorphisms \{\mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \simeq \mathcal{M} \otimes V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x\} defines a tensor functor \mathbf{Rep}(\check{G}_q) \to \mathrm{Vect}_X. This functor is a point of \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X) (q-Hecke eigenvalue determination). Conversely, the Hecke correspondence sends every q-local system \mathcal{L}_q to a q-\mathcal{D}-module \mathbb{L}_q^{-1}(\mathcal{L}_q) on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}.

Step 3: Uniqueness from rigidity. Suppose \mathbb{L}_q and \mathbb{L}_q' both satisfy properties (1)--(3) of the q-Geometric Langlands conjecture. The composition \mathbb{L}_q' \circ \mathbb{L}_q^{-1} is a tensor auto-equivalence of \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X)) that preserves the tautological q-local system. By the rigidity of \tau, this auto-equivalence is uniquely isomorphic to the identity. \square
sec:q-opers-intro: This section turns to the spectral side of the conjecture and the canonical objects that realise it. It returns to the q-oper: a \check{G}_q-bundle on X, equipped with a reduction to the Borel subgroup and a q-flat connection in oper position. This object provides the rigid spectral data dual to the automorphic q-Hecke eigensheaves. The fibre functor maps every q-oper to a q-Hecke eigensheaf, with the eigenvalue determined by the oper coordinates, realising the abstract Tannakian mediation. Whereas the (G, q)-opers of Edward Frenkel and Nicolai Reshetikhin [frenkel-reshetikhin1998], Mina Aganagic, Edward Frenkel, and Andrei Okounkov [aganagic2018], and Peter Koroteev and Anton M. Zeitlin [koroteev-zeitlin2022] are meromorphic q-difference connections with respect to a multiplicative shift z \mapsto qz on \mathbb{P}^1 or \mathbb{C}^\times, the q-opers considered here replace that multiplicative shift by the contact-deformed differential d_q so that the Borel transversality condition remains defined on a compact curve X of genus g \ge 2.
conj:q-oper-hecke:
Conjecture q-Opers are q-Hecke eigensheaves. q-Hecke eigensheaves are constructed explicitly from q-opers. Every q-oper (\mathcal{P}_{\check{G}_q}, \nabla_q) \in \mathrm{Op}_{\check{G}_q}(X) defines a point \nabla_q \in \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X). The q-Geometric Langlands equivalence (q-GL conjecture) maps the corresponding skyscraper sheaf \delta_{\nabla_q} to a q-Hecke eigensheaf \mathcal{M}_{\nabla_q} on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X):

  \mathcal{M}_{\nabla_q} = \mathbb{L}_q^{-1}(\delta_{\nabla_q}).

The eigenvalue q-local system is the q-oper connection itself. For each point x \in X and dominant weight \lambda, the Hecke action yields

  \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}_{\nabla_q})
  \simeq
  \mathcal{M}_{\nabla_q} \otimes
  V_\lambda^{(q)}(\nabla_q)_x.

The transversality condition defining the q-oper ensures that \mathcal{M}_{\nabla_q} is irreducible as a q-\mathcal{D}-module. Transversality to the Borel subgroup prevents the existence of non-trivial sub-q-\mathcal{D}-modules.
rem:q-oper-hecke-sketch:
Remark Proof sketch: q-opers produce eigensheaves. The q-oper abla_q defines a point in \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X). Under the conjectured equivalence \mathbb{L}_q (q-GL conjecture), its pre-image \mathcal{M}_{ abla_q} = \mathbb{L}_q^{-1}(\delta_{ abla_q}) is a q-\mathcal{D}-module on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}. Hecke compatibility (property (1) of the conjecture) immediately ensures that \mathcal{M}_{ abla_q} is an eigensheaf with eigenvalue abla_q.

To prove irreducibility, suppose \mathcal{N} \subset \mathcal{M}_{ abla_q} is a non-zero sub-q-\mathcal{D}-module. The equivalence \mathbb{L}_q maps \mathcal{N} to a non-zero subsheaf of \delta_{ abla_q}. Because skyscraper sheaves are simple, \mathbb{L}_q(\mathcal{N}) = \delta_{ abla_q}. The equivalence then forces \mathcal{N} = \mathcal{M}_{ abla_q}.

Alternatively, irreducibility follows directly from the q-oper transversality condition. A proper sub-q-\mathcal{D}-module would induce a abla_q-invariant sub-bundle compatible with the Borel reduction. This contradicts the non-vanishing requirement \mathrm{pr}_{-\alpha_i}( abla_q mod \check{\mathfrak{b}}_q) eq 0. \square
sec:q-gl-classical-limit-intro: With the conjecture stated on the non-torsion locus, this section checks that the q \to 1 degeneration recovers familiar geometry and reads the resulting structure physically. The classical-limit conjecture asserts that specialising at q = 1 recovers the classical Geometric Langlands equivalence of Beilinson–Drinfeld, and an accompanying remark sketches how the degeneration of q-opers and q-Hecke eigensheaves recovers their classical counterparts. A further remark refines this picture: the obstruction classes \kappa_n vanish identically at q = 1 but persist on the full non-torsion locus, forcing the correspondence to be intrinsically q-deformed away from the classical fibre. The section closes with two interpretive remarks, which read the equivalence as the observability condition that the fibre functor \tau supplies for a quantum observable universe.
conj:q-gl-classical-limit:
Conjecture Classical limit of the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence. Any q-deformation of Geometric Langlands must reduce to the classical Beilinson–Drinfeld equivalence \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}} at q = 1; the q-correspondence passes this consistency check, and it does so through three compatible limits of its defining data (differential, Hecke, and dual-group). Accordingly, as q \to 1 in the \mathbb{G}_m-family, the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence recovers the classical Geometric Langlands equivalence:

  \lim_{q \to 1} \mathbb{L}_q =  \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}}
  \colon \mathcal{D}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))
  \xrightarrow{ \sim }
  \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}}(X)).

This degeneration factors into three limits:

  1. Differential limit: d_q \to d and d_q^2 \to 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2). Quantum flat connections become classical flat connections. Quantum local systems become classical local systems.
  2. Hecke limit: The Hecke relation (T-q)(T+q^{-1}) = 0 degenerates to (T-1)(T+1) = 0. This recovers the symmetric group action. Quantum Hecke operators become classical Hecke correspondences.
  3. Dual group limit: \check{G}_q = G_{q^{-1}}^\vee \to G^\vee = \check{G} as the quantum deformation vanishes.
rem:q-gl-classical-limit-sketch:
Remark Proof sketch for classical recovery. Each component of the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence represents a continuous deformation in q. The q \to 1 limit of each yields its classical counterpart.

q-Local systems. At q = 1, the q-monodromy condition (q-local system) becomes \mathcal{L}_1(\varrho) = \mathrm{id} for contractible \varrho. This is the classical condition that monodromy depends only on the homotopy class. Hence \mathrm{LocSys}_{G_1}(X) = \mathrm{LocSys}_G(X).

q-\mathcal{D}-modules. The q-flatness equation \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q becomes \nabla^2 = 0 at q=1. The category \mathcal{D}_q\text{-}\mathrm{mod} specialises to the classical category of \mathcal{D}-modules.

q-Hecke operators. The eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} degenerate to 1 and -1. The q-Hecke correspondence degenerates to the classical Hecke correspondence, and the factorisation defect [\mathbf{T}_x, \mathbf{T}_y] = O(q-1) vanishes.

q-Opers. The transversality condition is q-independent and persists at q = 1, where q-opers become classical opers.

Because each ingredient converges and the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q is uniquely determined by the fibre functor (fibre-functor mediation), the limit \mathbb{L}_1 = \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}} emerges as the unique equivalence compatible with classical Hecke operators and the identity fibre functor. \square
rem:q-gl-obstruction-classical-compatibi:
Remark Perpetual obstruction and the classical limit. The perpetual obstruction (obstruction calculation) and the classical limit (classical recovery) coexist compatibly, rendering the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence a singular deformation of the classical theory.

The point q = 1 is the universal torsion point. It belongs to \mu_n for every n \geq 1. At q = 1, the q-exterior derivative reduces to d, the obstruction d_q^2 vanishes, and the q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q = 0. Classical flatness \nabla^2 = 0 holds, as does the Beilinson--Drinfeld equivalence \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}}. However, q = 1 lies in \mu_\infty, outside the non-torsion locus \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}} where \mathbb{L}_q is well-defined. The classical correspondence is the degenerate fibre of the \mathbb{G}_m-family, not a generic point.

Let q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}} and \chi(A) \neq 0. The obstruction class \kappa_0 is non-trivial at density-1 Kummer levels. Thus, q-flatness is strictly stronger than classical flatness. The moduli \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X) is a proper subspace of the classical prediction. Three observations resolve this:

  1. The classical limit q \to 1 approaches a boundary point of the parameter space \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}. The point q = 1 lies in the closure of the open complement of \mu_\infty.
  2. As q \to 1, the (q-1)-factor in the q-flatness equation \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q forces \nabla_q^2 \to 0, even though \mathcal{F}_q remains non-zero. The vanishing prefactor screens the curvature.
  3. The Kummer constraint (property (4) of the q-GL conjecture) encodes this singular behaviour. The equivalence degenerates precisely at roots of unity. The classical limit is the universal degeneration.

The classical theory is recovered by specialisation to this singular point.
rem:q-gl-physical-interpretation:
Remark Physical interpretation of q-Geometric Langlands. This section interprets the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence physically within the QOU framework.

The category \mathcal{D}_q\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}) encodes q-deformed gauge theory on the brane. G_q-bundles are read as field configurations, q-\mathcal{D}-modules as quantum states, and q-Hecke operators as particle insertions that modify the gauge field at a point. The q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q is the field strength. The d_q^2 \neq 0 obstruction forces this curvature to be non-zero.

The category \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}) encodes the q-deformed matter sector. The \check{G}_q-local systems carry parallel transport data for matter fields. The Langlands dual \check{G}_q controls the allowed representations. The Kummer filtration on \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q} stratifies the matter sector by the divisibility of the obstruction class \kappa_0.

The functor \mathbb{L}_q asserts categorically that the gauge and matter sectors carry equivalent information. This duality arises because a single aether parameter q controls both the braiding and the differential calculus. A q-Hecke eigensheaf is a quantum state that responds to gauge field modifications by scalar multiplication by a q-local system. It represents a particle carrying a definite charge under \check{G}_q.
rem:q-gl-automorphic-observability:
Remark Automorphic--spectral duality as observability. The fibre-functor mediation conjecture connects the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence to the observability axiom of the QOU (quantum observable universe). Concretely, the correspondence is a dictionary between gauge configurations and matter content, and observability forces that dictionary to be unique.

The observability condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 constrains the adjoint representation and thereby the fibre functor \tau. Because \tau uniquely determines \mathbb{L}_q, the automorphic--spectral duality follows from observability. Relaxing observability reintroduces adjoint cohomology. The obstruction classes \kappa_n interact with this cohomology to produce additional obstructions to the equivalence (fibre-functor rigidity).

The rigidity of \tau guarantees that the Langlands equivalence is unique. The Kummer filtration on \kappa_0 (Kummer filtration) determines the arithmetic locus where \mathbb{L}_q is well-defined.

The q-deformation as quantum correction. The passage from \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}} to \mathbb{L}_q is controlled by (q-1), which plays the role of \hbar_q (q-Planck constant). The q-Geometric Langlands correspondence is the fully quantum-corrected gauge/matter duality, with the classical Langlands programme recovered in the semiclassical limit \hbar_q \to 0.

Uniqueness from observability. Observability is what makes the q-Langlands equivalence unique: it forces a single dual pairing between gauge and matter.
sec:spectral-trace-preamble:
Having identified the unit particle as a cohomological defect, these defects are counted across the spectral fiber. The maximal ideals of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathcal{B}) act as the primes of the quantum geometry. Counting them with appropriate weights yields q-analogs of classical arithmetic functions. Defect-counting on the geometric side is dual to spectral decomposition on the algebraic side.

Tannaka--Krein duality bridges these two perspectives. The category of localized representations at defects is equivalent to the category of comodules over the Hopf algebra reconstructed from the Reeb spectrum. This equivalence converts the geometric sum over defects into a spectral trace over Reeb eigenvalues, providing the non-commutative analog of the classical explicit formula from prime number theory.
